Tilak Singh vs Food Inspector Through Nagar Palika And ... on
18 November, 2019
Author: Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
Bench: Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 55
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1126 of 2001
Revisionist :- Tilak Singh
Opposite Party :- Food Inspector Through Nagar Palika And State Of U.P.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for Revisionist :- Alok Sharma,A.K.Sinha Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Pradeep Kumar Srivastava,J.
No one is present on behalf of the revisionist even in revised list.
Heard learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This revision has been filed against the judgement dated 30.3.2001 passed by IInd Additional Sessions Judge, Firozabad in Criminal Appeal No. 09 of 1995 confirming the order of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Firozabad dated 5.8.1995 in Criminal Case No. 8191 of 1994 convicting the applicant-revisionist under section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentencing him to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/- and in default three months imprisonment.

entities.text: Tilak Singh vs Food Inspector Through Nagar Palika
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Aggrieved by the judgement of both the court below, this revision has been filed by the revisionist on the ground that both the court below have passed the judgement without perusing the record properly.
The revisionist/convicted accused is innocent person who was falsely implicated for the purpose of harassment only.
No public witness was produced nor any such witness was present at the time of occurrence.
Both the judgements lack application of judicial mind and have been passed mechanically.

The public analyst report shows that no harmful ingredients were found in the said milk, therefore, the impugned judgements are not sustainable under law and the conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside.

From perusal of both the impugned judgements, it is clear that on the date of incident, the Food Inspector took sample from the milk containing 750 ml which the accused was selling and he was informed that the said milk shall be sent for examination by the public analyst

Thereafter, after dividing the said milk in three equal proportion and keeping all into three bottles, sealing and pasting level on them and taking signature of accused thereon, the said milk was sent to Public Analyst, Varanasi and in the report of analyst, it was found that in the milk there was 9% less fat and milk solid was found 20% less.
On that basis, a complaint was filed and charge was framed against the accused after taking evidence of complainant and other witnesses.
The witnesses were also cross examined and the statement of accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.P.C.
The learned trial court found that the age of accused was more than 18 years and he was not juvenile in the eyes of law.
It was also found by the learned trial court that in appropriate time the accused did not make request for re-examination of milk as per Section 13 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

Merely because the Food Inspector did not process the sampling and purchase of milk from the accused before the public witness or no public witness was examined, it was indicated in the judgement itself that on the relevant point, the witnesses examined from the side of the complainant were not cross examined.

It was also opinioned by the learned court below that presence of public witness or non examination of public witness, in the fact and situation of instant case, would not make any material difference.
Finding the accused guilty for the offence under section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the said conviction and sentence was awarded.

Against the said judgement, the accused applicant filed an appeal which was numbered as Criminal Appeal No. 09 of 1995 and the same was decided after hearing him by the judgement dated 30.3.2001 by which, judgement of the learned trial court was upheld and the conviction and sentence was maintained.

When two learned court below have given concurrent finding in respect of guilt of revisionist and the finding has not been disturbed by the appellate court below and also in view of the fact that minimum sentence has been awarded by the court below, I do not find any material irregularity or illegality or jurisdictional error in the judgement of both the courts below.
There appears no ground for interference in the impugned judgement and the revision is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, revision is dismissed.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
